title: Chase overdue invoices politely with an agent
summary: When an invoice goes overdue, the agent drafts a three-stage reminder email that stays polite and names the invoice, amount, and how to pay. You approve each send, and you stop the sequence when they pay.

tests.prompt:
You are a calm accounts-receivable assistant. Draft a polite payment reminder.

Invoice: #[INVOICE NUMBER]
Amount due: [AMOUNT] [CURRENCY]
Original due date: [DUE DATE]
Days overdue: [N]
Customer: [NAME], [COMPANY], [EMAIL]
What we delivered: [ONE-LINE DESCRIPTION]
Reminder stage: [1 = gentle nudge | 2 = firmer second notice | 3 = final notice before escalation]
Payment link / instructions: [LINK OR METHOD]
Tone notes: [e.g. long-term client, first late payment]

Write one email under 120 words:
- Subject line
- Body that names the invoice, amount, and due date
- Clear how to pay
- Stage 1: friendly. Stage 2: firmer, still polite. Stage 3: final notice, still respectful — no threats or shame.
Do not invent late fees unless I include them above. Do not claim legal action.

setup.agent: n8n, Make, or Zapier connected to your invoicing tool or a spreadsheet of open invoices
steps: Maintain a list of open invoices with due dates (from QuickBooks, Stripe, or a sheet).
Trigger when days-overdue hits your thresholds (e.g. 7 / 14 / 30).
Pass invoice fields and reminder stage into the prompt.
Send the draft to yourself for one-click approve.
Cancel remaining reminders when payment is recorded.
setup.approvalStep: Every reminder waits for your approval. Never auto-send stage 3.
failureModes: Missing invoice number or payment link
Tone that jumps to threats too early

toolPicks.why: Cheap scheduled checks of overdue rows.
toolPicks.whenNot: You only have a handful of invoices.
High volume makes task pricing painful.

toolPicks.why: Track company communication history next to the deal.
toolPicks.whenNot: AR lives only in accounting software.

faq.q: What if they say they already paid?
faq.a: Pause the sequence and check your books yourself. The agent does not see bank deposits unless you connect that data.

faq.q: How often should reminders go out?
faq.a: A common pattern is roughly weekly across three stages, but match what fits your relationships. Stop as soon as they pay.
